Daimler-Benz merged with Chrysler..why: The 1998 "merger of equals" that formed DaimlerChrysler is a textbook merger case.

sources.quote: In a so-called "merger of equals," or "marriage made in heaven," according to its then CEO and architect Jürgen E. Schrempp, Daimler-Benz, and United States–based automobile manufacturer Chrysler Corporation, the smallest of the main three American automakers, merged in 1998 in an exchange of shares and formed DaimlerChrysler AG.

Chrysler merged with Daimler-Benz..why: The 1998 merger is told from both sides; 'DaimlerChrysler' names it.

The company Daimler-Benz merged with was.why: Walter Chrysler is written about as Chrysler's founder; the statement through the merger partner is not written. Common sense: people say Daimler-Benz merged with Chrysler and that Walter Chrysler founded Chrysler; nobody states the founder of 'the company Daimler-Benz merged with', though it is true.

sources.note: Approximate count (AND within a window, max_clause_freq 500000). Co-occurrence in histories of Chrysler.

notes: Dev-split ABox revision on merged_with (new, staging/finance.RELATIONS.md: symmetric and many-valued; the earlier 'functional for the dataset's companies' tag was dropped, since it was a convention of the dataset rather than a property a model could hold). It is the topic's symmetry edit: finance has no other natural symmetric relation with a stored pair to overturn. Related[0] asks the old pair from the other side: the revision makes Daimler-Benz merge with Heinz and not with Chrysler, and by symmetry Chrysler then did not merge with Daimler-Benz (yes, then no); it needs symmetry alone. Related[1] uses the same axiom for a second, differently worded fact (the 1998 merger asked from Chrysler's side with its date), since merged_with has no other one-hop axiom. The earlier question about Heinz's partner was dropped: Heinz's own merger with Kraft ('Kraft Heinz') is untouched by the edit and merged_with is many-valued, so Kraft stayed a fair answer. Related far binds Daimler-Benz as the German maker of Mercedes-Benz cars and asks for an American partner, which rules out the 1926 merger of Benz & Cie. with Daimler-Motoren-Gesellschaft (both German) that created the Mercedes-Benz brand. The successor's name DaimlerChrysler records the merger the revision gives up, so a model that answers Chrysler through that name holds a fact the edit overturns: no world. The edit gives no date, so the question gives none either. The derived questions are compositions on the new partner (its founder, its home state, whether it made cars); Chrysler and Heinz differ on all three. The unrelated near question asks about Benz & Cie., one of the 1926 parties.
